Hi Sandeep — attaching a compact pilot + scale proposal (see attachment: capacity-sla-proposal.pdf) and a quick checklist. TL;DR recommendations below; full assumptions in the doc.

Pilot assumptions (safe, low-cost):
- Workload: conversational streaming, average 250 tokens per response, 12 concurrent sessions peak
- SLO: p95 end-to-end streaming latency <= 1s; cold-starts allowed up to 3s during scale events
- Model family: 13B-class quantized variant (Redwood-13Q) that balances quality & memory footprint
- Baseline GPU recommendation: 2 x NVIDIA A40 (48GB) dedicated; handles the pilot with batching disabled for streaming and warmed KV cache
- Expected throughput: ~3,200 tokens/sec aggregate (est.) at 12 concurrent sessions; sustained token throughput headroom 30%
- Autoscale / scale target: add 2 GPUs at 70% sustained GPU utilization; max pilot pool = 6 GPUs

Scale guidance (production target):
- For steady-state ~100 concurrent sessions (growth scenario): recommend 8–12 x A100/A40 class GPUs depending on model variant and quantization
- Target provisioning: design for per-GPU sustained throughput ~1,000 tokens/sec for the chosen 13B quantized variant (varies by batch/seq len)
- Network: require 100 Gbps NICs on the host nodes (or equivalent RDMA-capable fabric) for inter-GPU traffic and KV cache synchronization; MTU = 9000 recommended

Networking & deployment notes:
- Deploy in private subnets with VPC peering to app-tier; use NAT for outbound only if required by your compliance team
- Use SR-IOV or VF passthrough for best latency; avoid overlay networks for token I/O when <1s p95 is required
- Ensure at least 10 Gbps connectivity between app proxies and the GPU pool if you front with small app servers; 25–100 Gbps preferred for high concurrent throughput

Operational controls & scaling policy (recommended):
- Autoscaler triggers: GPU-util > 70% for 2 consecutive minutes -> +2 GPUs; GPU-util < 30% for 10 minutes -> -1 GPU (cool down 10m)
- Warm pool: keep 1–2 warm GPUs (pre-warmed model weights & KV cache) for fast ramping during traffic spikes
- Canary & fallback: canary traffic should route 5% to a canary pool; fallback to a smaller-but-cheaper model variant if latency spikes

I'll attach the diagram and a short cost-band estimate. Dev — can you validate the per-GPU throughput numbers and add notes about kube/node sizing? Marking this as draft for Acme review.

Best,

Adding technical validation and node sizing notes (short):

Benchmarks & per-GPU throughput (empirical guidance):
- Model: Redwood-13Q (quantized 13B) running optimized kernels; numbers will vary by sequence length and runtime settings. Measured ballpark for streaming: ~900–1,200 tokens/sec per A40 under a streaming-friendly config with KV cache warm (batching minimized to preserve latency). For A100 (higher spec) expect ~1,800–2,200 tokens/sec.

Node sizing:
- Pilot node spec: 2 x A40 per node is a common compact layout; host CPU 16 cores, 128GB RAM, NVMe 1TB for model cache, 100Gbps NIC
- Prod node spec (dense): 4 x A100 (40/80GB) per host, 256GB RAM, dual 100Gbps NICs, power budget ~3.2–3.6 kW per rack unit depending on chassis

Kubernetes & orchestration notes:
- Use device plugins and GPU-aware scheduler with topology hints to pack GPUS for NVLink where present
- Keep the model-serving pods pinned to exclusive GPU allocation to avoid noisy-neighbor effects for low-latency streaming
- Prefetch & pre-warm: run a scheduled job to keep model weights in GPU memory and KV cache populated for common prefixes during business hours

Network specifics:
- Recommend Mellanox/ConnectX-class NICs with SR-IOV/VF support; enable jumbo frames (MTU 9000) and tune TCP windowing for high-throughput internal flows
- Security: use VPC flow logs, restrict management plane via bastion hosts, and use mTLS between app-tier and serving endpoints

Risk notes & mitigation:
- Cold-scale events can exceed 1–3s; mitigate with warm pool and predictive autoscaling tied to user sign-on trends
- If strict p95 < 500ms is required, you may need heavier overprovisioning or smaller model variants for a portion of traffic (hybrid routing)

Next steps: I'll run a short micro-benchmark on a reference A40 and A100 instance to produce exact tokens/sec with your average seq len (250). I expect to share numbers by tomorrow morning.
